name: Framer Motion Spring Stagger
description: React + Framer Motion (motion/react) implementation of a spring-driven row stagger. AnimatePresence handles enter/exit; motion.div components animate via stiffness/damping with per-element delay. Same choreography as lib-gsap-spring-stagger but expressed as React components, so the scene can compose into a larger React tree.

stiffness.description: Spring stiffness for the entrance transition. Higher = snappier.

stagger_s.description: Per-element delay (seconds), passed to transition.delay = i * stagger_s.

exit_y.description: Y translation (px) on exit. Negative = upward.

when_to_use: React scenes where motion is part of a larger component tree
Spring physics that adapt to interruption (Framer Motion handles re-targeting natively)
AnimatePresence-driven enter/exit — the library handles the unmount-coordination CSS can't
when_to_avoid: Vanilla HTML prototypes — use lib-gsap-spring-stagger to skip React boot cost
Sequences requiring per-frame numeric tweens on non-DOM values — GSAP's onUpdate is more direct than driving a React state
ai_guidance: No capture adapter required — Framer Motion rides on rAF + performance.now(), both already patched by virtual time. When emitting the prototype, pin React via ?deps=react@19.0.0 on every dependent esm.sh URL — without this, motion/react imports a second copy of React and useContext fails. See the prototype_template for the exact importmap shape.
